<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 650 480" width="650" height="480">
  <!-- White background rect -->
  <rect width="650" height="480" fill="#ffffff" />

  <!-- Title above the field -->
  <text x="325" y="35" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Uniform magnetic field into the page</text>

  <!-- Dashed rectangle representing the magnetic field region -->
  <!-- Left edge at x=200, Right edge at x=500, Top at y=70, Bottom at y=330 -->
  <rect x="200" y="70" width="300" height="260" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="6,4" />

  <!-- Regular grid of 'x' marks inside the region (avoiding the semicircular path) -->
  <!-- Grid columns: x = 230, 270, 310, 350, 390, 430, 470 -->
  <!-- Grid rows: y = 95, 135, 175, 215, 255, 295 -->
  <!-- We omit or shift 'x' marks that would fall directly on the semicircle of radius 110 centered at (200, 200) -->
  <g font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#000000" text-anchor="middle">
    <!-- Row y=95 -->
    <text x="230" y="100">×</text><text x="270" y="100">×</text><text x="310" y="100">×</text><text x="350" y="100">×</text><text x="390" y="100">×</text><text x="430" y="100">×</text><text x="470" y="100">×</text>
    <!-- Row y=135 -->
    <text x="230" y="140">×</text><text x="270" y="140">×</text><text x="310" y="140">×</text><text x="350" y="140">×</text><text x="390" y="140">×</text><text x="430" y="140">×</text><text x="470" y="140">×</text>
    <!-- Row y=175 (center y=200, so skip close ones) -->
    <text x="230" y="180">×</text><text x="270" y="180">×</text><text x="350" y="180">×</text><text x="390" y="180">×</text><text x="430" y="180">×</text><text x="470" y="180">×</text>
    <!-- Row y=215 (center y=200, skip close ones) -->
    <text x="230" y="220">×</text><text x="270" y="220">×</text><text x="350" y="220">×</text><text x="390" y="220">×</text><text x="430" y="220">×</text><text x="470" y="220">×</text>
    <!-- Row y=255 -->
    <text x="230" y="260">×</text><text x="270" y="260">×</text><text x="310" y="260">×</text><text x="350" y="260">×</text><text x="390" y="260">×</text><text x="430" y="260">×</text><text x="470" y="260">×</text>
    <!-- Row y=295 -->
    <text x="230" y="300">×</text><text x="270" y="300">×</text><text x="310" y="300">×</text><text x="350" y="300">×</text><text x="390" y="300">×</text><text x="430" y="300">×</text><text x="470" y="300">×</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Path of the electron -->
  <!-- Straight entry: from x=80, y=200 to x=200, y=200 -->
  <!-- Semicircle inside: from (200,200) down to (200,420)? Wait, radius r=110. Center=(200,200). -->
  <!-- Semicircle goes from (200,200) downwards to (200, 420)? But bottom of field is at y=330. -->
  <!-- Let's check geometry: If radius r=110, and center is at left edge x=200, y=200: -->
  <!-- Then semicircle goes from (200, 200) down through (310, 310) to (200, 420). -->
  <!-- But wait! The prompt says "leaves the field". If the field ends at y=330, a semicircle of r=110 goes down to y=310 inside the field! -->
  <!-- Ah, let's verify: diameter is along the left edge from y=200 to y=420? No, left edge is from y=70 to y=330. -->
  <!-- If center is at (200, 200), semicircle goes downwards, so it spans y=200 to y=310. That fits entirely inside the field (y=70 to y=330). -->
  <!-- Then at y=310, x returns to 200? Wait. Semicircle starting at (200,200) going downwards and ending at (200,310)? No, a semicircle starts at one end of a diameter and ends at the other end. -->
  <!-- If diameter is vertical from (200, 90) to (200, 310), then the semicircle curves to the RIGHT! -->
  <!-- Let's re-read: "curves downwards, which is correct for a negative charge, and leaves the field moving to the left along a line below where it entered." -->
  <!-- Ah! If it enters horizontally moving right at y=200, and curves downwards and leaves moving LEFT, then the entry point is (200, 200) and exit point is, say, (200, 310) with a horizontal tangent? -->
  <!-- Wait, if it enters horizontally (tangent to circle at top), the circle goes downwards. A circle tangent to a horizontal line at the top and curving downwards has its center directly below the top point! -->
  <!-- Let's set Center C at (200 + r, 200)? No, "The centre of the semicircle is on the left edge of the field." -->
  <!-- If center C is on the left edge (x=200), and entry is at top of semicircle: then top of semicircle is (200, 200). Center must be at (200, 200 + r)? No, if top is (200,200) and center is below it, say at (200, 310), then the semicircle goes from (200,200) down to (200,420)? That doesn't curve right. -->
  <!-- Standard physics problem geometry: -->
  <!-- Electron enters at left edge, say at (200, 200) moving right. Inside field, force is downwards (Lorentz force $v \times B$). So it curves downwards. -->
  <!-- If center of circular path is at C, and it enters at (200,200) moving right, the radius vector from C to entry point (200,200) must point upwards (or at some angle). -->
  <!-- Let's check standard diagram for bubble chamber / magnetic deflection: -->
  <!-- Uniform field pointing INTO page ($\otimes$). Negative charge moving RIGHT. -->
  <!-- $F = q (v \times B)$. Since $q$ is negative, $F$ is opposite to $v \times B$. -->
  <!-- $v$ is right $(\hat{i})$, $B$ is into page $(-\hat{k})$. $v \times B = (\hat{i}) \times (-\hat{k}) = -\hat{j}$ (downwards). -->
  <!-- Since charge is negative, force $F = -e (-\hat{j}) = +\hat{j}$ (UPWARDS)? Wait! -->
  <!-- Let's re-verify: $F = q(v \times B)$. For electron, $q = -e$. -->
  <!-- $v = v \hat{i}$, $B = -B \hat{k}$. -->
  <!-- $v \times B = v(-B) (\hat{i} \times \hat{k}) = -vB (-\hat{j}) = vB \hat{j}$ (upwards). -->
  <!-- Therefore $F = (-e)(vB \hat{j}) = -e vB \hat$ (DOWNWARDS). Correct! Force is downwards. -->
  <!-- If force is downwards, the center of the circular path is BELOW the path. -->
  <!-- The electron enters at the left boundary moving right. As it enters, it immediately curves downwards. -->
  <!-- So the entry point is at the TOP of its circular trajectory! -->
  <!-- If the entry point is at the top of the trajectory, say at (200, 200), and the center C is directly below it, at (200, 200 + r), then the semicircle goes from (200, 200) curving down-right to the bottommost point (200 + r, 200 + r), and then curving up-left back to (200 + 2r, 200)! -->
  <!-- Let's check this: -->
  <!-- Entry point: (200, 200), moving right. -->
  <!-- Center: C = (200 + r, 200), where r is radius. Wait! If C is at (200+r, 200), then the distance from C(200+r, 200) to entry point (200, 200) is r, and the vector points LEFT ($- \hat{i}$). -->
  <!-- At entry point (200, 200), radius vector is $-\hat{i}$ (pointing left from center to entry). Velocity is $+\hat{i}$ (right). Dot product is 0, so velocity is perpendicular to radius! Perfect. -->
  <!-- As it moves into the field (x > 200), it follows a semicircle centered at C = (200+r, 200). -->
  <!-- Let's trace the semicircle from angle $\theta = \pi$ to $\theta = 0$ (or rather, from $-\pi/2$ to $+\pi/2$)? -->
  <!-- Let's use parametric equations for center C = (310, 200) [so r = 110]: -->
  <!-- Entry at (200, 200), which is C + r(-1, 0) = (310 - 110, 200) = (200, 200). -->
  <!-- As angle goes from $\pi$ (left, i.e., (200,200)) through $3\pi/2$ (bottom, i.e., (310, 310)) to $2\pi$ (right, i.e., (420, 200))? Wait, that goes back to the left edge? -->
  <!-- Let's check: from $\theta = \pi$ to $\theta = 0$ (clockwise): -->
  <!-- $\theta = \pi$: (200, 200) - entry, moving right? Wait, at $\theta = \pi$, tangent is downwards or upwards? -->
  <!-- Let's test standard circle: $x = 310 + 110 \cos\theta$, $y = 200 + 110 \sin\theta$. -->
  <!-- At $\theta = \pi$: $x = 310 - 110 = 200$, $y = 200$. Velocity vector is tangent, which is $(-110\sin\theta, 110\cos\theta)|_{\pi} = (0, -110)$ (vertical). That's vertical, not horizontal! -->
  <!-- We want horizontal entry at (200, 200). -->
  <!-- So at entry (200, 200), velocity is horizontal ($+\hat{i}$). Therefore the radius vector must be vertical ($\pm \hat{j}$). -->
  <!-- Since the center is on the left edge of the field (x = 200), and the path curves downwards, let's place the center C at **(200, 310)** (so x = 200, y = 310, with r = 110). -->
  <!-- Let's check this configuration: -->
  <!-- Center C = (200, 310). -->
  <!-- Radius r = 110. -->
  <!-- Entry point on left edge (x = 200): Let's see where a circle of radius 110 centered at (200, 310) intersects x = 200. -->
  <!-- Equation: $(x - 200)^2 + (y - 310)^2 = 110^2$. -->
  <!-- If $x = 200$, then $(y - 310)^2 = 110^2 \implies y = 310 \pm 110$. -->
  <!-- So $y = 420$ and $y = 200$! -->
  <!-- Wow, look at that! The points on the left edge ($x = 200$) are $(200, 200)$ and $(200, 420)$. -->
  <!-- Let's check the semicircle between $(200, 200)$ and $(200, 420)$ on the side where $x \ge 200$: -->
  <!-- At $y = 200$, $x = 200$. The radius vector from C(200, 310) to entry (200, 200) is $(0, -110)$ (pointing straight UP). -->
  <!-- The velocity is horizontal to the RIGHT ($+\hat{i}$). Since radius is $-\hat{j}$ and velocity is $+\hat{i}$, $\text{radius} \cdot \text{velocity} = 0$ (perpendicular). -->
  <!-- As the electron moves into the field ($x > 200$), it follows the semicircle to the right. -->
  <!-- The semicircle goes from $(200, 200)$, reaches its rightmost point at $x = 200 + r = 310, y = 310$, and returns to the left edge at $(200, 420)$! -->
  <!-- Wait, let's check the exit point: $(200, 420)$. At $(200, 420)$, the radius vector from C(200, 310) is $(0, +110)$ (pointing straight DOWN). -->
  <!-- The velocity is tangent to the circle, pointing to the LEFT ($-\hat{i}$). -->
  <!-- This matches the prompt perfectly: -->
  <!-- "leaves the field moving to the left along a line below where it entered." -->
  <!-- Entry at $y = 200$, exit at $y = 420$ (which is below $y = 200$). -->
  <!-- Let's check if the field region spans this vertically: -->
  <!-- Field rect is from $y = 70$ to $y = 330$? Wait! If exit is at $y = 420$, that is below $y = 330$. -->
  <!-- Let's adjust the field rectangle and coordinates so everything fits nicely inside the field! -->

  <!-- Let's redesign coordinates: -->
  <!-- Let the magnetic field rectangle be from x = 200 to x = 520, and y = 70 to y = 370. -->
  <!-- Let radius r = 100. -->
  <!-- Let Center C be at (200 + 100, 200)? Wait, prompt: "The centre of the semicircle is on the left edge of the field." -->
  <!-- Left edge of field is at x = 200. So center C must have x = 200. -->
  <!-- Let C = (200, 250). Radius r = 80. -->
  <!-- Then the circle is $(x - 200)^2 + (y - 250)^2 = 80^2$. -->
  <!-- Intersection with left edge x = 200 gives $y = 250 \pm 80$, i.e., $y = 170$ and $y = 330$. -->
  <!-- Let's check this: -->
  <!-- 1. Entry at $(200, 170)$ moving right ($+\hat{i}$): -->
  <!--    Radius vector from C(200, 250) to $(200, 170)$ is $(0, -80)$ (pointing UP). -->
  <!--    Velocity is right ($+\hat{i}$). Perpendicular! -->
  <!--    As it enters at $y = 170$, force is downwards, so it curves downwards into the field ($x > 200$). -->
  <!-- 2. Semicircle: goes from $(200, 170)$, reaches rightmost point at $(200 + 80, 250) = (280, 250)$, and returns to left edge at $(200, 330)$. -->
  <!-- 3. Exit at $(200, 330)$ moving left ($-\hat{i}$): -->
  <!--    Radius vector from C(200, 250) to $(200, 330)$ is $(0, +80)$ (pointing DOWN). -->
  <!--    Velocity is left ($-\hat{i}$). Perpendicular! -->
  <!--    It leaves the field moving to the left along the line $y = 330$, which is below the entry line $y = 170$. -->
  <!-- 4. Let's check field boundaries: -->
  <!--    Field x: from 200 to 450. (Semicircle reaches max x = 280, so 450 is plenty of room). -->
  <!--    Field y: from 100 to 360. (Entry at 170, exit at 330, bottom of semicircle at 330. Fits easily in $y \in [100, 360]$). -->

  <!-- Let's refine the exact coordinates with r = 90 for a nice clear diagram: -->
  <!-- Left edge of field: x = 200 -->
  <!-- Right edge of field: x = 480 -->
  <!-- Top of field: y = 80 -->
  <!-- Bottom of field: y = 380 -->
  
  <!-- Center C: (200, 230) -->
  <!-- Radius r = 90 -->
  <!-- Entry point: (200, 140) [since 230 - 90 = 140] -->
  <!-- Exit point: (200, 320) [since 230 + 90 = 320] -->
  <!-- Rightmost point of semicircle: (290, 230) [since 200 + 90 = 290] -->

  <!-- Let's check straight path segments: -->
  <!-- Entry straight line: from x = 90, y = 140 to x = 200, y = 140. -->
  <!-- Exit straight line: from x = 200, y = 320 to x = 90, y = 320. -->

  <!-- Semicircle arc: -->
  <!-- Starts at (200, 140), goes through (290, 230) to (200, 320). -->
  <!-- SVG path command for a semicircle from (200, 140) to (200, 320) with radius 90 and sweep-flag 1 (clockwise): -->
  <!-- M 200 140 A 90 90 0 0 1 200 320 -->
  <!-- Let's verify sweep: from y=140 to y=320 going via x=290 (right). Yes, clockwise arc from top to bottom on the right side has sweep-flag = 1. -->

  <!-- Center C dot and label: -->
  <!-- C is at (200, 230). Draw a solid circle at (200, 230) with r = 3. -->
  <!-- Radius line: from (200, 230) to (290, 230). Label it 'r' above the line. -->

  <!-- Let's check grid 'x' marks again for this geometry (C=(200,230), r=90, arc inside x in [200, 290], y in [140, 320]): -->
  <!-- Field rect: x from 200 to 480, y from 80 to 380. -->
  <!-- Grid columns inside field: x = 225, 260, 295, 330, 365, 400, 435, 470 -->
  <!-- Grid rows inside field: y = 105, 145, 185, 225, 265, 305, 345 -->

  <!-- Straight entry line: -->
  <line x1="90" y1="140" x2="200" y2="140" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.8" />
  <!-- Arrow on entry line pointing right -->
  <polygon points="150,135 162,140 150,145" fill="#000000" />

  <!-- Straight exit line: -->
  <line x1="90" y1="320" x2="200" y2="320" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.8" />
  <!-- Arrow on exit line pointing left -->
  <polygon points="140,315 128,320 140,325" fill="#000000" />

  <!-- Semicircular path inside the field -->
  <path d="M 200 140 A 90 90 0 0 1 200 320" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.8" />
  <!-- Arrow on semicircle pointing downwards/leftwards (around y=230, x=290) -->
  <!-- Tangent at (290, 230) going south is downwards. Let's put an arrowhead around y=230, x=290 -->
  <polygon points="285,235 290,247 295,235" fill="#000000" />

  <!-- Centre of the semicircle -->
  <circle cx="200" cy="230" r="3.5" fill="#000000" />

  <!-- Radius line from centre (200, 230) to rightmost point (290, 230) -->
  <line x1="200" y1="230" x2="290" y2="230" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-dasharray="4,3" />

  <!-- Labels -->
  <!-- electron label near entry -->
  <text x="95" y="125" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-style="italic">electron</text>
  
  <!-- speed v label with vector arrow or just v -->
  <text x="110" y="158" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-style="italic">speed v</text>

  <!-- radius r label above the radius line -->
  <text x="245" y="222" font-family="Times New Roman, serif" font-size="16" font-style="italic" text-anchor="middle">r</text>

  <!-- Field boundary rectangle (drawn again cleanly or kept from above) -->
  <!-- We already have the dashed rect at x=200, y=80, w=280, h=300 -->
  <rect x="200" y="80" width="280" height="300" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="6,4" />

  <!-- Grid of 'x' marks, carefully positioned to avoid path (arc bounded by x in [200,290], y in [140,320]) -->
  <g font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#000000" text-anchor="middle">
    <!-- Row y = 105 (above arc) -->
    <text x="225" y="110">×</text><text x="260" y="110">×</text><text x="295" y="110">×</text><text x="330" y="110">×</text><text x="365" y="110">×</text><text x="400" y="110">×</text><text x="435" y="110">×</text><text x="470" y="110">×</text>

    <!-- Row y = 145 (near top entry, x=200..290 has arc) -->
    <!-- arc at y=145: (200-200)^2 + (145-230)^2 = 85^2 = 7225 -> x = 200 + sqrt(8100 - 7225) = 200 + sqrt(875) = 200 + 29.6 = 229.6 -->
    <!-- So for x <= 230 inside arc. Marks at x >= 240 are safe. -->
    <text x="245" y="150">×</text><text x="280" y="150">×</text><text x="315" y="150">×</text><text x="350" y="150">×</text><text x="385" y="150">×</text><text x="420" y="150">×</text><text x="455" y="150">×</text>

    <!-- Row y = 185 -->
    <!-- arc at y=185: (185-230)^2 = 45^2 = 2025. 8100 - 2025 = 6075 -> sqrt = 77.9 -> x = 277.9 -->
    <!-- Marks at x >= 295 are safe. -->
    <text x="310" y="190">×</text><text x="345" y="190">×</text><text x="380" y="190">×</text><text x="415" y="190">×</text><text x="450" y="190">×</text>

    <!-- Row y = 225 (near center y=230) -->
    <!-- arc at y=225: (225-230)^2 = 25. 8100 - 25 = 8075 -> sqrt = 89.8 -> x = 289.8 -->
    <!-- Marks at x >= 300 are safe. -->
    <text x="310" y="230">×</text><text x="345" y="230">×</text><text x="380" y="230">×</text><text x="415" y="230">×</text><text x="450" y="230">×</text>

    <!-- Row y = 265 -->
    <!-- same as y=185 -->
    <text x="310" y="270">×</text><text x="345" y="270">×</text><text x="380" y="270">×</text><text x="415" y="270">×</text><text x="450" y="270">×</text>

    <!-- Row y = 305 -->
    <!-- same as y=145 -->
    <text x="245" y="310">×</text><text x="280" y="310">×</text><text x="315" y="310">×</text><text x="350" y="310">×</text><text x="385" y="310">×</text><text x="420" y="310">×</text><text x="455" y="310">×</text>

    <!-- Row y = 345 (below arc) -->
    <text x="225" y="350">×</text><text x="260" y="350">×</text><text x="295" y="350">×</text><text x="330" y="350">×</text><text x="365" y="350">×</text><text x="400" y="350">×</text><text x="435" y="350">×</text><text x="470" y="350">×</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Caption below figure -->
  <text x="90" y="420" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold">Fig. 3.1</text>
</svg>
